blocks.text: Gala Precision Engineering (GPEL) is a Rs 314 crore (FY26) maker of small engineered metal parts in three families: Disc and Strip Springs including Gallock wedge-lock washers (DSS), Coil and Spiral Springs (CSS), and Special Fastening Solutions (SFS), i.e. high-tensile studs, anchor bolts, hex bolts and nuts [F] (AR2026 p.49) [F] (AR2026 p.161). It buys steel sheet, coil, wire and rod, and blanks, forms, coils, heat-treats, grinds, thread-rolls and machines them into 800+ SKUs for about 175 active customers in 25+ countries [F] (AR2026 p.49) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). It earns money as a build-to-print or catalogue supplier. Management says about 85% of output is customised to customer drawings and 10-15% is standard DIN parts sold through fastener distributors [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Pricing is cost-plus with raw-material pass-through after a 3-6 month lag [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).

Manufacturing is at two Wada (Palghar, Maharashtra) plants and one fastener plant at SIPCOT Vallam-Vadagal near Chennai, which ramped from August 2025 [F] (AR2026 p.83) [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).

There are only two audited post-listing years, eight earnings calls' worth of guidance history, and no prospectus in our evidence set. Long-run facts (customer history, pre-2020 margins) therefore rest on screener data and management statements rather than offer-document disclosure [AI].

blocks.text: Driver classification [AI]: thesis 1 is company-specific. Thesis 2 is company-specific, riding a structural wind and renewables cycle. Theses 3 and 4 are structural (qualification barriers, India cost arbitrage). Thesis 5 is company-specific and partly one-off, since it is IPO cash. Thesis 6 is cyclical, tied to wind installations and OEM schedules. Thesis 7 is company-specific but temporary.

subsections.title: Bear thesis: reasons not to own it

items: 1. Valuation is disconnected from every model scenario. At Rs 1,103 the stock is 72% above the bull-case DCF value of Rs 306.8 and 467% above the base case of Rs 194.7. The reverse DCF needs 103.4% annual sales growth for five years [F] (NUMBERS).
2. Growth does not turn into cash. Three-year CFO/PAT is 0.35x and three-year FCF is minus Rs 56 cr [F] (NUMBERS). FY26 CFO was Rs 10.17 cr on PAT of Rs 35.48 cr [F] (AR2026 p.163-164).

3. Working capital is structurally heavy. Inventory of Rs 89.43 cr and receivables of Rs 81.53 cr together equal 54% of sales [F] (AR2026 p.159) [E]. Management now says working capital will stay at similar levels pending a KPMG study [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

4. The margin guide has been missed for two years. Management guided 17-19% repeatedly [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026), but delivered 16.51% in FY26 and 16.31% in Q1 FY27 [F] (PPT Aug 2026).

5. A patent suit hits a growth product. Nord-Lock AB is suing over Gallock wedge-lock washers. Rs 2.00 cr sits in contingent liabilities, but the plaintiffs reserve the right to claim on total infringing sales [F] (AR2026 p.149-150).

6. Q1 FY27 shows strain. A Rs 3 cr+ dispatch was held over a customer's payment delay [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Revenue was down 20% QoQ to Rs 75.38 cr [F] (NUMBERS). On our arithmetic, SFS revenue was roughly flat against the H1 FY26 quarterly average (see segments) [E].

7. Hedging policy was changed at the same time as an Rs 3.23 cr forex loss. Forward cover was cut from 70% to 40% of export collections [MC] (CALL Jun 2026), but the annual report still describes 65-70% hedging [F] (AR2026 p.139). Euro net unhedged exposure is Rs 18.00 cr [F] (AR2026 p.139).

8. The capacity runway is short and the next step needs land not yet owned. Wada has no land left [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). The 10.15-acre Wada parcel is only at MoU and due-diligence stage, with Rs 40-45 cr capex mostly next year [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

9. Governance has small but real frictions: an exchange fine for NRC composition in FY25 [F] (AR2026 p.84); 3,00,000 ESOPs at Rs 530 to two whole-time directors, valued at zero volatility so no expense is booked [F] (AR2026 p.134-136); and income-tax proceedings at company premises concluded on 24 Aug 2026 [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS).

10. US exposure is gated by a 50% Section 232 tariff on springs and fasteners [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). America was only 6% of Q1 FY27 sales, against 10-14% cited in FY26 calls [F] (PPT Aug 2026) [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).

Is Chennai incremental revenue or relocated revenue? Chennai makes studs as well as bolts [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Part of its ramp may be stud volume moving from Wada, so the 'Rs 80 cr from Chennai' figure may overstate net new revenue [AI]. The other side: wind OEM bolt price agreements are genuinely new [MC] (CALL Feb 2026).

Is cash conversion a growth phase or the business model? FY20-FY24 CFO was Rs 9-16 cr a year on PAT of Rs 1-24 cr [F] (NUMBERS). Inventory days on screener's basis have stayed above 250 for seven years [F] (NUMBERS). Our read is that this is structural to a 800-SKU, minimum-order-quantity model [AI]. Bulls would point to the KPMG study [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

Is the margin dip forex or something else? Management blames a 1% forex loss of Rs 3.23 cr [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). But labour (job-work) charges rose to 13.6% of sales from 12.2%, and freight to 2.7% from 2.0% [F] (AR2026 p.192) [E]. Also, Rs 2.11 cr of forward-contract discount sits in other income, below EBITDA [F] (AR2026 p.189). The market may be both over-penalising the reported dip and under-appreciating the creep in outsourcing cost [AI].

Is concentration falling? The largest customer fell from 23.60% to 15.97% of revenue [F] (AR2026 p.199). That is about Rs 56 cr to Rs 50 cr, so the top customer shrank in absolute terms [E]. The improvement is partly diversification and partly a key account softening [AI].

Is the market pricing optionality the DCF cannot see, such as aerospace, electrolysers or offshore wind? Management says aerospace has no short-term impact [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) and offshore wind is targeted at 10% of fastener sales [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Neither is large enough to bridge the gap to the reverse DCF [AI].

blocks.text: Our read [AI] is that the consensus story, a niche Indian precision-spring franchise graduating into a large fastener market, is directionally supported by the numbers: revenue doubled from Rs 145 cr in FY22 to Rs 314 cr in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS). But it is priced as if growth were free. Every incremental rupee of sales has needed roughly 0.5 rupees of working capital plus capex. FY25-FY26 FCF was minus Rs 59 cr against Rs 62 cr of PAT [F] (NUMBERS) [E]. Margins have not expanded with scale (opm 19% FY24 to 17% FY26) [F] (NUMBERS). The variant view is therefore not 'bad business' but 'good business, capital-hungry, priced for a capital-light compounder'. The thesis would change only if working-capital days fall materially after the KPMG exercise, or if Chennai lifts group margins into the 17-19% band while CFO/PAT moves above 0.7x [AI].

blocks.text: Both subsidiaries are immaterial: combined total assets are about Rs 0.03 cr, and they are unaudited and management-certified [F] (AR2026 p.155). There is a disclosure inconsistency. The auditor says one foreign subsidiary is being wound up [F] (AR2026 p.155), and Crisil said winding-up had been initiated [F] (RATING). Yet AOC-1 states 'subsidiaries liquidated or sold during the year: NIL' [F] (AR2026 p.94). Both can be true if winding-up is incomplete; the documents do not say [AI].

The springs business is decades old, but the fastener franchise behind the growth story is young. SFS began in 2018 [MC] (PPT Aug 2026). Bolts and nuts only began supplying in Q4 FY26 [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Chennai first shipped in mid-2025 [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). Offshore wind started in FY26 [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Roughly a third of revenue, and most of the incremental growth, comes from a product line with fewer than eight years of history and no full cycle through a wind downturn [AI]. New products are 30-35% of the order book [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

items: 1. Customer drawing or DIN standard, then in-house tool design and development; tooling is held to 5-10 microns for disc springs [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) [F] (PPT Aug 2026).

2. Raw material: steel sheet and strip (DSS, wedge-lock washers), wire (CSS), rod (SFS) [F] (PPT Aug 2026). Some grades are imported against steel-mill minimum order quantities, which drives inventory [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). FY26 CIF imports were Rs 13.98 cr [F] (AR2026 p.61).
3. Forming: blanking and forming (discs), coiling (springs), forging and thread rolling (fasteners); forging investment made at Chennai [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [F] (PPT Aug 2026).
4. Heat treatment, shot peening, grinding, CNC machining [F] (PPT Aug 2026).

5. Surface treatment: hot-dip galvanising was in-sourced at Chennai in Jul 2026, because some customers required it in-house [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Other coatings are partly outsourced [AI] based on job-work costs.
6. Kitting: studs and bolts are made in-house; nuts and washers are bought in and kitted, at 15-20% of sales [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).
7. Qualification: plant audit, PPAP sample approval, small share of business, then share-of-business ramp over 12-24 months [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).
8. Delivery to OEM factories or warehouses, billed direct; distributors get standard parts [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

blocks.text: Value is captured at qualification, not at the forge [AI]. Fasteners are 3-4% of wind-turbine cost [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), so customers switch for commodity-manager cost targets (5-20% savings goals) only after audits and safety approvals [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Once designed in, a supplier holds share for years: 80-82% of sales come from existing parts at existing customers [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). Gross margin proxy, defined as revenue less materials consumed and the change in inventories, was 59.6% in FY26 and 58.4% in FY25 [F] (AR2026 p.161-162) [E]. That is a large conversion-value share, but labour charges, power, stores and freight then absorb most of it [AI].

Labour charges, which we read as contract labour and job work, rose 47% to Rs 42.86 cr. That is faster than revenue growth of 32% [F] (AR2026 p.192) [E]. Fixed-asset turnover is about 3.0x [F] (NUMBERS), in line with management's 3x mature asset-turn rule [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). Management's own sizing for new capacity is capex of 35-40% of target sales [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Add working-capital needs of 140+ days [F] (NUMBERS) and the business is capital-moderate on fixed assets but capital-heavy overall [AI].

blocks.text: Most differentiated [AI]: custom disc springs and safety-critical springs such as retractor springs, where tooling precision, fatigue life and approvals matter. Disc springs were developed with German universities [MC] (PPT Aug 2026). Most commodity-like [AI]: standard DIN disc springs and wedge-lock washers sold through distributors, and build-to-print studs and bolts against domestic competitors. On these, management concedes entry pricing below market [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Management's statement that all product groups earn a similar 17-19% EBITDA [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) is not testable, because segment margins are not disclosed [F] (AR2026 p.198-199).

The audited accounts report a single operating segment, 'Springs, Parts, Fasteners and Assemblies' [F] (AR2026 p.198-199). Product splits exist only as percentages in calls, the rating note and the presentation. Rupee figures below are our derivations [E] unless a rupee figure was stated.

Discrepancy, not reconciled: Crisil puts FY25 SFS at 32% of revenue (~Rs 76 cr) [F] (RATING). Management's 'Rs 108 cr, +64%' for FY26 implies an FY25 base of ~Rs 66 cr (~28%) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [E]. FY25 DSS/CSS growth rates cannot be derived reliably either way.
Segment margins: not disclosed. Management asserts similar margins across product groups and end-markets [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).

items: SFS. Management attributes FY26 growth (+64%) to wallet-share gains, bolts from Chennai and new customers [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Our read [AI]: H1 FY26 SFS was Rs 44 cr (+84%) [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) with almost no Chennai sales (Rs 0.82 cr dispatched by September) [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). That gives a Wada SFS run-rate of ~Rs 21-22 cr a quarter [E]. Q1 FY27 SFS of Rs 22.3 cr already includes Chennai output of ~Rs 4-5 cr a month [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). This implies Wada stud sales fell sharply, or that stud production moved to Chennai [E] [AI]. Q1 SFS growth versus a ~Rs 22 cr H1 FY26 quarterly average looks roughly flat [E], partly explained by the Rs 3 cr+ held dispatch [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

DSS. Driven by exports, which rose from 44% to 51% of DSS revenue in Q3 FY26 [MC] (CALL Feb 2026), and European share gains [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Our read [AI]: the best-quality growth in the group, from the Wada plant at ~80-85% utilisation [MC] (CALL Jun 2026), so constrained by capacity.

CSS. 'Steady demand' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Mix share drifted from 19% to 17% [F] (RATING) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Our read [AI]: the low-growth, automotive-exposed segment, where NHK and Stumpp Schuele are larger incumbents.

blocks.text: Nothing here is tender-driven. SFS for wind is schedule- and program-driven by a handful of OEMs, hence the most order-like and cyclical. DSS and CSS are run-rate businesses fed by monthly schedules and three-to-six-month forecasts [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [AI].

Management maintains 20-25% growth and says Q1 is typically 20-22% of annual revenue [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Arithmetic check [E]: Rs 75.38 cr as 20-22% of the year implies Rs 343-377 cr. Applying 20-25% growth to Rs 314.30 cr gives Rs 377-393 cr. The two statements overlap only at the edge, so the guide requires Q1 to be at most ~20% of the year.

blocks.text: Only two years are audited, so no multi-year CAGR is computable. Management's regional shares within exports vary by call. In Nov 2025: US 10-12%, Europe 18-19%, RoW 3% [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). In Feb 2026: Europe ~20%, US ~14% [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). In Q1 FY27: Europe 25%, America 6% [F] (PPT Aug 2026). These are not reconciled. The direction (Europe up, US down) coincides with the 50% Section 232 tariff on springs and fasteners [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [AI].

The export share fell from 37.6% to 35.5% because domestic wind and Chennai SFS grew faster, not because exports shrank [F] (AR2026 p.199) [AI]. Management's model is 'launch in India, then take global', with exports held at 35-40% [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). The mix shift is therefore a lag effect of new fastener lines, not a strategic retreat [AI].

FY26 foreign-exchange earnings were Rs 111.51 cr and outgo Rs 2.34 cr; CIF imports were Rs 13.98 cr [F] (AR2026 p.61). At year-end, net unhedged exposure was EUR Rs 18.00 cr and USD Rs 8.02 cr. FY26 had a net forex loss of Rs 3.23 cr in other expenses and forward discount income of Rs 2.11 cr in other income [F] (AR2026 p.189) [F] (AR2026 p.192).

Hedging policy discrepancy, not reconciled. The annual report: the company hedges 65-70% of export collections [F] (AR2026 p.139). Feb 2026 call: cover reduced to 30-50% [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). May and Aug 2026 calls: cut from 70% to 40% [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Lower cover raises P&L sensitivity to EUR/INR.

blocks.text: Illustrative share arithmetic only [E]. GPEL's FY26 SFS revenue of Rs 108 cr is below 1% of the Indian SFS market at any exchange rate above ~Rs 16.4/USD. It is a fraction of 1% of the global market. DSS at ~Rs 154 cr is ~7.7% of management's own Rs 2,000 cr addressable figure. These ratios say nothing about achievable revenue. Most of the 'market' is commodity, automotive or construction fasteners GPEL does not make. Access requires per-customer qualification. Capacity, not demand, caps revenue at roughly Rs 445-480 cr nameplate [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) [AI].

A better frame [AI]: (number of qualified OEM programs) x (share of business per program) x (customer program volume). Management gives the inputs qualitatively. There are 175 active customers. 10-15% of growth a year comes from new customers [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). SFS share-of-business is 10-25% per customer, with a ceiling of 30-35% [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Customer spend is Rs 5-10 cr a year per disc-spring customer and Rs 50-500 cr per fastener customer [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). On those claims, a handful of fastener customers moving 5-10 points of share is worth more than the entire DSS addressable growth [E] [AI].

Supply is fragmented, with European, Japanese and Indian specialists by niche [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). Demand is concentrated in wind, where a handful of OEMs control volume. items: Upside the market may miss [AI]: DSS's European share gains (+31% in Q1) are the highest-quality growth, and they are being masked by SFS noise.

Downside the market may miss [AI]: Chennai revenue is partly relocated stud output, and FY23 earnings were flattered by other income. That makes the 5-year PAT CAGR (77%) misleading next to the 3-year 13.4% [F] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: On our model data, year-5 sales range from Rs 464 cr (bear) to Rs 954 cr (bull), with EBITDA of Rs 60-181 cr [F] (NUMBERS). The constraint across the range is not demand but capital. Each step needs land, Rs 40-45 cr of capex [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), and working capital at ~140 days [F] (NUMBERS). The outcome that would justify today's price, sustained 100%+ growth, is outside both management's guidance and the company's history [AI].

At Rs 1,103 the shares trade 3.6x the bull-case DCF value (Rs 306.8), 5.7x the base (Rs 194.7) and 14x the bear (Rs 77.7) [F] (NUMBERS) [E]. The reverse DCF requires 103.4% five-year sales CAGR against 23.9% delivered [F] (NUMBERS). We issue no rating or price target.

Three things [AI]. First, a 14.9% WACC applied to a business whose cash flows are back-ended. Second, heavy working capital and capex that consume the operating cash of growth. Third, a market narrative (import substitution, wind, fasteners TAM) that is being capitalised as if it were cash-generative today. The first is debatable. The second is evidenced [F] (NUMBERS). The third is a sentiment premium [AI].
